summary:
The Southern Even-fingered Gecko once navigated the broken stone districts and takyr flatlands of central Asia, a small, smooth-scaled creature threading through the arid landscapes of Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan at elevations barely above sea level. Sporadic and elusive by nature, it carved out a quiet existence in one of the world's most unforgiving terrains.

Its world did not survive the plow. Decades of agricultural expansion drowned and fragmented its habitat, and the very place where this gecko was first discovered now lies beneath a reservoir. Encounter rates collapsed from one animal per few hectares to just four individuals found across an entire decade of searching. What was once a living presence in the stones has become nearly a silence.
